text:
maria: Starting bring-up for apac-south2 GPU cluster (spot-heavy). running bootstrap v2.3.1 now. asking for quick eyes on failures.
ajay: 👍 what symptoms?
maria: nodes showing NotReady after cloud-init completes. kubelet crashloop on driver probe.
noah: any kernel mismatch logs?
maria: attaching short excerpt: 
```
Jul 12 03:12:41 instance-12 kubelet[1234]: E07012 03:12:41.123456 kubelet.go:xyz] Failed to start Kubelet: failed to load modules: nvidia: modprobe failed (exit status 1)
Jul 12 03:12:41 instance-12 cloud-init[456]: /var/log/nvidia-installer.log: Error: kernel headers not found for 5.10.0-37-generic
```
ajay: hmm looks like AMI has kernel 5.10 but driver package expects 5.15. which GPU driver tar are we pushing?
maria: bootstrap uses driver bundle `nv-driver-470.129` from artifact-store; image base was baked with `nvidia-utils-450` during image bake. clearly a mismatch.
tiffany: oh, image mismatch. we should have pinned driver version during bake step. did the bake pipeline pick latest?
maria: yes - bake pipeline picked latest tag without enforcement.
noah: two paths: roll back bootstrap to use 450-compatible driver or rebuild AMI with 470 kernel headers. which is faster?
ajay: rolling back bootstrap script to install 450 is fastest for handoff. but 450 doesn't support the A100 variant we're targeting for right performance — it's a temporary degraded perf path.
maria: cost/priority question: apac-south2 was requested for immediate capacity — do we accept degraded perf for now? customer pilot needs GPUs but can tolerate slightly lower throughput.
tiffany: agree to degraded perf temporarily. create a short-lived dedicated pool with 450 drivers, mark as non-default routing, and run smoke tests.
maria: starting one-off job to install 450. patching bootstrap user-data to `DRIVER_VERSION=450.140` now.
sre-bot: deploy request created: deploy/infra-bootstrap/apac-south2/patch-450 at 1782508052 by maria
noah: also seeing autoscaler reporting 0 GPU capacity after node join: `node.kubernetes.io/gpu` label missing. kubelet didn't register device plugin due to driver failure.
maria: yes device-plugin pod crashed with error: `failed to detect MIG devices`
```
I07012 03:13:02 device-plugin.go:67] failed to get device list: nvidia-smi returned exit code 2
```
ajay: once drivers install, device-plugin should come up. if not, we can force-roll device-plugin image to v0.10 which has more conservative probing.
tiffany: can we stage traffic to our eu fallback until this settles? routing policy for apac-south2 should prefer eu when capacity low. current policy still treats apac as higher priority.
maria: I toggled service-routing to prefer eu for non-prod; prod still points to apac. done.
devops-tooling: autoscaler event: scaled up 4 nodes (requested 6), 2 failed boot due to driver timeout, remaining 2 NotReady
noah: sounds like we need to increase kubelet timeout for driver install during bootstrap (cloud-init pipelining). quick fix: add sleep + retry around driver install step in user-data. longer term: bake AMI.
maria: patch applied. re-triggering bootstrap on failed instances.
sre-bot: instance /i-0a1b2c3d re-provisioned (retry #2)
ajay: while this runs, can we validate networking? I saw intermittent MTU errors on the overlay during earlier test — could also slow driver download causing timeouts.
maria: ran net-check script, outgoing bandwidth fine but MTU mismatch on eth0 (1500) vs CNI (9000) for nv-driver blob chunks -> occasional fragmentation but shouldn't break kernel headers fetch.
offline: @noah did you kick off the driver-hosted-s3? not sure if blob path is signed properly.
noah: yes signed URL expiry was 10s; we increased to 5m now. was expiring mid-download for larger packages.
maria: good catch. re-running installs.
(twenty minutes pass)
sre-bot: smoke-tests/infra/apac-south2 -> partial-success (device-plugin up on 2 nodes, 2 nodes still NotReady)
maria: progress. the two remaining failures are the spot-backed instances that received early evictions (preempted) during install. spot eviction rate is higher in apac-south2 atm — cloud provider advisory posted ~1h ago.
ajay: can we request on-demand fallback for those two? cheaper to spin a small on-demand pool than repeat spots.
tiffany: approved. opened capacity request to infra-dedicated team.
devops-tooling: capacity request acked: creating 2 on-demand instances in apac-south2 (d-sku)
maria: once on-demand come up, we'll label them `bringup-temp=true` and handoff to platform for routing test.
noah: final checklist before handoff: 1) verify device-plugin on all ready nodes 2) run perf smoke (gpt-2 1k token) 3) confirm routing and fallback policies 4) create rollback note and cost estimate for temp on-demand nodes.
maria: doing those now. ETA 20m.
ajay: ping me for handoff — I'll own the routing verification.
maria: handoff note: after driver mismatch + signed-url expiry + spot preemptions we patched bootstrap to pin 450 driver, extended signed-url ttl, added driver-install retries, and toggled non-prod routing to eu fallback. created on-demand temp capacity.
tiffany: thanks. please paste final commands to re-run bootstrap for audit.
maria: command used: `gcloud compute instances add-metadata i-xxxx --metadata-from-file=user-data=bootstrap-450.sh && /usr/local/bin/infra-trigger-reprovision i-xxxx`
noah: cost note: estimated extra cost for 2 on-demand d-sku nodes ~ $1.6k/mo pro-rated, added to incident ticket #INC-2026-347.
maria: handing off to ajay & tiffany for routing + perf validation. i'll stay on post for 30m.
ajay: taking over. thanks @maria. :thumbsup:
tiffany: will validate perf and confirm we can move pilot traffic. :white_check_mark:
maria: closing thread for now, will update INC-2026-347 with final status. :party:
